steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Your friend left so soon? She won't even stay for dinner?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Mm... she had urgent business. She couldn't stay.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Even as a child, you never brought friends over. Here I thought I could drop in to see what she's like.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I don't know if we even—count as friends, really...
Seeing the dejected Ning Yin, the old man tries to think of something to say, but can't. He simply reaches over and brushes a leaf off her shoulder.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Almost time to move. Plenty of things still on your plate, eh?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: What about you, Grandfather?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Heheh, for days I was all raring to go home. Now that we're about to, I look around at our little garden and I think 'oh, if only I could stay'.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Do you remember? It was here in this pavilion we laid out some sand, and grabbed a stick, and I taught you how to write one stroke at a time.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You said by next year, you'd be writing all the estate couplets for us. Then you spent two months with me learning, and after that you had to give up.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: But by next year, you really did write me a couplet.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: 'Bountiful blooms and a full moon; may joy last forever.'

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I'm surprised you still remember, Grandfather.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: How could I forget... Ah, another year, another Mid-Autumn. How quickly the days pass.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: The two of us haven't chewed the fat like this in the longest, have we? Grandfather to granddaughter.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Mm. I've been out constantly, and you're always occupied with guests. We hardly have the chance to meet.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: The whole family's leaving the capital, after all. Quite the headache.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: But things will settle down once we're back in Langyi, and we'll have plenty of time to chat along the way.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Are you almost done writing that book of yours?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Grandfather, I don't... think I can go back to Langyi with you.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: When did you make up your mind?
Ning Yin shakes her head softly. She falls a few steps back.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: You're returning home, Grandfather, like a leaf returns to its root. It's human nature, the whole family sympathizes. But the journey is meandering enough to make us worried.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: The Nings are bursting with talent. Everyone's work forms a cornerstone of Yan. Compared to them, I really am the lone choice to accompany you back.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: But frankly, I was always a distant orphan from Langyi anyway. It was because you took such pity on me that I could spend these decades at the Ning manor.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: If I go now to Langyi, I go back to where my long-gone parents once lived.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: That was your thinking... when you asked to accompany me home?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Grandfather... that was my thinking.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: It all seemed to fall into place. I almost managed to convince myself.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: But I've spent the last few days on a farewell tour of sorts around Baizao's streets, so I can finish up the Baizao Cuisine & Food Culture somehow.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: And I realized, all my memories are of this city.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I can clearly recall what year we planted that persimmon tree in the courtyard, and when its fruits make for the best wine.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: And every restaurant of every road and alley, and what their chefs are like, and how many different ways you can cook each dish.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: All of a sudden, it hit me that... this very city, moreso than the Ning manor, feels like my home.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: ...That's on me. That's on me for not asking you how you feel. I've been nothing but me this whole time.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Grandfather, you're my one and only family. You've always been since I was little.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I really did want to go back home with you at first, but the reason I'm set on staying in Baizao now... is you as well, Grandfather.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Is it?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Mm-hm.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: When I first joined the Imperial Historical Cabinet to compile annals, there was one thing I could never puzzle out.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: At some specific point in Yan's millennia of history, out of nowhere, the written word proliferated and education became for all. Even the earliest of the tablets we were studying only went back to that period.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: So I thought, in that period, someone must have pushed for those changes. But I flipped through practically all the material we had, and I couldn't find a single clue.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I had this strange feeling that, there in Yan's history, one person seemed to be missing.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Then one day, I met someone strange at a Go club, who told me the story of 'that person'.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I thought he was just a yarn-spinning storyteller at first, but as I further researched, I gradually found all his stories to be corroborated.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: According to him, 'she' was a gentle person who gave her heart and soul, her blood and sweat to the wellbeing of the people. And she gave too much... But how could someone as good as her fail to leave her name in our annals?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: That was when I realized that a history book isn't a container, but a sieve. The stories that stay behind are few and far between.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Grandfather... I want to record your story. But then I look back, and it dawns on me that for all the years I've spent with you, I can't even write with any clarity about...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: About what—kind of person you are.
Ning Yin finally lifts her head, and meets the old man's eyes.
She waits for his reply, his answer to her unspoken question.
She's waited for so long.

steps.name: Judicial Officer A
steps.text: Who goes there!

steps.name: Judicial Officer B
steps.text: Who goes where?

steps.name: Judicial Officer A
steps.text: Tch... Thought I heard something.

steps.name: Judicial Officer A
steps.text: It's all the bizarre cases these days. Makes me feel like someone's going to barge in any moment and wreak havoc.

steps.name: Judicial Officer B
steps.text: This is the Judicial Review Office. What kind of miscreant would break in here?

steps.name: Judicial Officer B
steps.text: Quit jumping at ghosts. Guard duty's almost over, and then we can clock out and head home.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Just wait a sec and then enter through the front... say you're here to report a case, then find a floor map on the way to the waiting room...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: The window in the waiting room yesterday faces north, the Judicial entrance faces south, behind is a high perimeter wall.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Lin Qingyan's office is sec—third floor... get out the window, climb up the sprinkler pipes, and no one should notice me.

spans.text: floor... get out the window, climb up the sprinkler pipes, and no one should notice me.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Ta ma de! Once I find her I'm gonna sock her in the...!

spans.text: Once I find her I'm gonna sock her in the...!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Lin Qingyan?!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Blaze?!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What are you here for?!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What am I here for? I'm here to get YOU back!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Where'd your old court uniform go?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I resigned.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Then went back to the restaurant, couldn't find you, and worried you might be up to something stupid, so thank you for confirming that fear.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Now let's find somewhere else to talk!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You're telling me that all those years, Gu Quan was staying at the Ning manor?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: But how did you find out...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Never you mind that. Now, can you tell me exactly what that means?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Minister Ning's involvement in the Gu Quan case runs deeper than I ever thought. He was clearly hiding something in his previous testimony.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I did suspect he was the perpetrator, but going by Mo Bufu's testimony, when Gu Quan was sent to death row in the fallout of the old case, Ning Shu was the one who got him out. Knowing that...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: He wouldn't have a motive to try and get him killed again.

spans.text: He wouldn't have a motive to try and get him killed

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: And the most key thing... I had no idea before that Yu Cheng had contact with Gu Quan so early on.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Whatever's connecting this string of events, it's likely more complicated than anything I've imagined.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: See, I'm still curious. All those years ago, my dad came to Baizao on his own—and what the hell for?

spans.text: See, I'm still curious. All those years ago, my dad came to Baizao on his own—

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yes, that's the key question...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: (Blaze has no clue about the two lives Gu Quan lived... If he was a fall guy in that incident, then why would he return to Baizao a dozen years after the fact and plant himself in the middle of the maelstrom?)

spans.text: (Blaze has no clue about the two lives Gu Quan lived... If he
a fall guy in that incident, then why would he return to Baizao a dozen years after the fact and plant himself in the middle of the maelstrom?)

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: (Ning Shu's position, Yu Cheng's scheme... We still can't draw an outline around any of these questions.)

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: (How should I let Blaze know...)

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hey, you know I can tell that look on your face?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: C'mon. What's our next move, exactly?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Blaze, about yesterday...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Forget about it. I know you 'it's-my-duty' types get the urge to do a little weird stuff now and then. Not my circus, I'm not arguing.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Just don't ever tell me any stupid crap like 'I'm sending you back for your safety' again, because—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You're still trying to ditch me!?!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Blaze, trust me, I will see this case through to the end... but you can't stick around in Baizao any longer than this.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Do as I said. Leave within two days, head to the Lungmen office first. But you can't stay there for too long either, so once you're reorganized, get back on the road straight away and leave Yan as soon as—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Over my dead body.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You don't trust me to keep investigating?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I mean, I do, but you're out of a rank, you're out of a job, how are you gonna investigate?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I'll think of something.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If Yu Cheng can resign and investigate in secret, then so can—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I have an idea.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Let's do this thing a little more thoroughly.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What's your plan?
Blaze pulls a letter from her pocket.
It's the chance Mo Bufu gave her, and now it's both of their chances.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Not like we're gonna get anywhere just running around town.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: We'll head to the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies, go straight to the True Lung, and ask him to explain all this.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty, the Ministry of Rites has drafted the official list of attendees for the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: To mark the occasion, Victoria, Leithanien, Laterano and other such nations have sent us their envoys with letters of celebration.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: For Your Imperial Majesty's perusal.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... *cough* *hack*...

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty... the Ministry of War and Sui Regulator have finished drawing up joint battleplans.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Also for Your Imperial Majesty's... *cough* *cough*... perusal.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: The Ministry of Revenue was not consulted on this battle's drain on labor and fiscal resources, nor on the postwar reparations. How were these battleplans drafted?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: I know you and the Ministry of Revenue are both very busy. The Ministry of War simply went to some small pains working out the manpower, the funding, the ration, and even the Ministry of Works's postwar repair expenses.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: And now you can read together with His Majesty, since we're having an audience and all.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Logistics are calculable, but how many of Yan's people will bleed in this war? Is that a bill you can work out so easily?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: So the Grand Tutor means to say, if you can't work it out, then no need to try?

steps.name: Voice Behind the Curtain
steps.text: It's autumn... How are the harvests in the north?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Dahuang has resumed production ASAP following the disaster. Our harvest this year is more or less on par with previous years.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Curtain
steps.text: In that case... what about next year?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty...

steps.name: Voice Behind the Curtain
steps.text: A life measured in years, yet the stress feels ancient. We're running out of time.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: This involves the livelihoods of all Yan's people. I ask that Your Imperial Majesty reconsider.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Grand Tutor, the Ministries have long discussed everything worth discussing. It's about time we made up our minds.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: His Majesty's decree is made. We simply await his proclamation at the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Curtain
steps.text: It's growing late. It looks to rain.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Curtain
steps.text: ...The two of you can leave.

steps.name: Grand Tutor & Grand Commandant
steps.text: May we be excused.
The man behind the curtain lifts his gaze—
In this desolate palace, three banquet seats lay set out in a row to his side, and one of them is truly showing its age.
Faintly, a sigh.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Aiyo, aiyo... Trust this rain to come from nowhere, I'm soaked...

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Autumn drizzles and cold snaps... We'll be out of fresh vegetables in a few days at this rate. I didn't even get to rustle up this year's winter clothes...

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Chef, I think we're forced to start our winter pickles now. Get your mess of stuff out of the storehouse as soon as—

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Chef...?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Blaze? Xingzhu? Where'd everybody go...?
The ever-lively kitchen is presently deserted, all the cookware tidied away. The cramped space seems a good bit wider like this.
The only presence is a pot of soup boiling on the stove.
